intended_object: The restriction (pullback) map induced by a continuous additive homomorphism f : A → B. It sends a ℚ/ℤ-valued character χ of B with open kernel to χ ∘ f, which is a character of A with open kernel, and it is a group homomorphism openKernel B → openKernel A. This is inferred from the docstring and from the `torsionRestrict` definition next to it.
explanation:
The forward map sends c to `dual f c`, which is c ∘ f. Its kernel is f⁻¹(ker c), so it is open because f is continuous. That is exactly the openness proof given. Additivity and preservation of zero come from `dual` being linear. So the definition is the standard contravariant map on open-kernel characters. It is an additive homomorphism, as it should be.

The generality is right. It only needs f to be a continuous additive homomorphism between topological abelian groups, which is the setting `openKernel` itself is defined in. Neither `openKernel` nor this restriction map exists in Mathlib, and Mathlib has no more general version of it.
